title: Astrocyte Biocomputing: Astrocytic Contributions to Neural Network Computation
abstract: arXiv:2611.17532v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conductors are critical for the performance of an orchestra even though they do not emit sound. Basic research and clinical studies in the last decade are revealing that astrocytes may be the "conductors" of the "orchestra" that is the brain network: astrocytes make up approximately $50\%$ of all brain cells but do not emit electrical signals. Nevertheless, they may play critical roles in important cognitive brain functions, specifically learning, memory, and information processing. Here we consider the implications of these discoveries for brain-inspired machine learning (ML), where analogy is typically drawn between neurons and their electrical interactions. We highlight specific algorithms for two key astrocyte characteristics. The first characteristic is the ability to link to and modulate thousands of synapses simultaneously. translated_title: 星形胶质细胞生物计算：星形胶质细胞对神经网络计算的贡献
translated_abstract: 指挥家对管弦乐队的演出至关重要，尽管他们自身并不发声。过去十年的基础研究和临床研究表明，星形胶质细胞可能是大脑网络这个“管弦乐队”的“指挥家”：星形胶质细胞约占全部脑细胞的50%，但并不发出电信号。然而，它们可能在重要的认知脑功能中发挥关键作用，特别是学习、记忆和信息处理。本文探讨了这些发现对脑启发机器学习（ML）的意义，在脑启发机器学习中，通常将神经元及其电相互作用进行类比。我们针对星形胶质细胞的两个关键特性提出了具体的算法。第一个特性是能够同时连接并调制数千个突触的能力。基于这一特性的模型实现了更快的训练速度，并使网络对噪声更加鲁棒……
tldr: 本文将星形胶质细胞（尤其是其同时连接并调制数千个突触的能力）的特性建模引入脑启发机器学习，实现了更快的训练速度和更强的噪声鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper incorporates astrocyte characteristics—particularly their ability to simultaneously link and modulate thousands of synapses—into brain-inspired machine learning, yielding faster training and improved robustness to noise.
